# Model owner vs. tenant as a per-unit occupancy type instead of a new role
## Context and Problem Statement
The project brief ([01-project-brief.md](../../01-project-brief.md)) separates two kinds of people who live in a unit:
- **Owners** see the condominium's expenses, supplier hires and budgets, and take part in decisions. - **Tenants** (~30% of the units in the reference building) can book common areas, report faults and read announcements. They **cannot** see financial information or take part in decisions.
The constitution ([00-constitucion.md](../../00-constitucion.md), PRINCIPIO-006) fixes the role set to exactly six roles: `Administrator`, `BoardMember`, `Resident`, `NonResidentOwner`, `Concierge` and `Supplier`. `Resident` covers both resident owners and tenants, and a new role cannot be added without amending the constitution.
The MVP features M5 (expense register) and M6 (supplier hires with visible justification), defined in [02-alcance.md](../../02-alcance.md), must be visible to owners and hidden from tenants. How do we enforce that distinction without breaking PRINCIPIO-006?
## Decision Drivers
- Comply with PRINCIPIO-006 and keep exactly six roles. - Hide financial data from tenants, which the brief treats as a hard access boundary. - Handle real-world cases: a person may own one unit and rent another, and occupancy changes over time (sale, end of lease). - Keep tenant isolation (PRINCIPIO-003) and the data retention rules (PRINCIPIO-004.5) straightforward to apply. - Keep the change small: one developer, 16 weeks.
## Considered Options
1. **`OccupancyType` attribute on the person–unit link** (`Owner` or `Tenant`). 2. **New `Tenant` role.** 3. **Owner flag on the person** (`IsOwner` on the user or person record). 4. **Restrict financial data to `NonResidentOwner` and `BoardMember` only.**
## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: **"`OccupancyType` attribute on the person–unit link"**. It is the only option that meets every driver without amending the constitution. Ownership is a fact about a person **and a specific unit**, not a property of a person's role in the system.
### Model
A `UnitOccupancy` entity links a person to a unit:
| Property | Type | Notes | |---|---|---| | `Id` | `Guid` | | | `CondominiumId` | `Guid` | Required. Filtered by the global query filter (PRINCIPIO-003) | | `UnitId` | `Guid` | | | `PersonId` | `Guid` | | | `OccupancyType` | `enum { Owner, Tenant }` | | | `StartDate` | `DateOnly` | First day of the occupancy (inclusive). An occupancy whose `StartDate` is after the current date in `America/Lima` is not active yet | | `EndDate` | `DateOnly?` | Last day of the occupancy (inclusive). `null` while no end date is known. The occupancy is **active** while `StartDate` is less than or equal to, and `EndDate` is `null` or greater than or equal to, the current date in `America/Lima`. A future `EndDate` may be registered |
### Rules
- **Financial access policy (`CanViewCondominiumFinancials`)** is granted to: - `Administrator` and `BoardMember`; - `NonResidentOwner` with at least one **active** `Owner` occupancy in the current condominium (re-audit RQ-A02); - `Resident` with at least one **active** `UnitOccupancy` where `OccupancyType = Owner` in the current condominium. - The policy is evaluated against the database on each request. It is never derived from a claim, so access is removed from the first request after the last active `Owner` occupancy ends (RN-016). - A `NonResidentOwner` may only have `Owner` occupancies. - A `Tenant` occupancy never grants financial access, even if the same person has another `Owner` occupancy in a different condominium. Access is always checked inside the current tenant. - When the last active occupancy of a person in a condominium ends, the `Resident` and `NonResidentOwner` roles are revoked there (RN-060). The 90-day retention period of PRINCIPIO-004.5 starts only when the person has neither active occupancies nor roles, from the later of the last `EndDate` and the last role revocation (RN-005). - Financial views show each expense with its receipt and the full supplier-hire file, never data about specific units or other residents (RN-036, RN-090, RN-041; audit C-03, re-audit RQ-A04).
### Consequences
- Good, because the role set stays exactly as PRINCIPIO-006 defines it, with no constitutional amendment. - Good, because it models mixed cases correctly: owning one unit while renting another, or several owners of the same unit. - Good, because the occupancy history keeps a dated record of who owned or rented each unit, which `DataRetentionJob` can use. - Bad, because authorization now depends on role **and** data, so `[Authorize(Roles = ...)]` alone is not enough. Every financial endpoint must use the named policy. - Bad, because the permissions matrix becomes more complex: rows for `Resident` must state the occupancy condition.
### Confirmation
- `docs/security/permissions-matrix.md` lists `Resident (Owner)` and `Resident (Tenant)` separately (as columns) for every financial resource. - Integration tests (xUnit) cover at least the following: - `ResidentTenant_CannotReadExpenses_Returns403` - `ResidentOwner_CanReadExpenses_Returns200` - `NonResidentOwner_CanReadSupplierHires_Returns200` - `ResidentOwner_AfterOccupancyEnds_CannotReadExpenses_Returns403` - `ResidentOwner_CrossTenantExpenses_Returns404` - Code review checks that no financial endpoint uses a role-only authorization attribute. - The users module (identity, authentication, roles) keeps line coverage at or above 90% (PRINCIPIO-010).
## Pros and Cons of the Options
### `OccupancyType` attribute on the person–unit link
- Good, because it complies with PRINCIPIO-006. - Good, because it represents ownership per unit and over time. - Neutral, because it adds one entity, which M1 (condominium registry) needs anyway to link people to units. - Bad, because it needs policy-based authorization and more tests.
### New `Tenant` role
- Good, because it uses simple role-based checks. - Bad, because it **violates PRINCIPIO-006**. It would need a constitutional amendment through a human-approved PR and ADR. - Bad, because a role is global to the user, so it cannot represent a person who owns one unit and rents another.
### Owner flag on the person
- Good, because it is the simplest change. - Bad, because it cannot represent different relationships with different units. - Bad, because it has no history. A sale or the end of a lease overwrites the value, and the record of when access ended is lost.
### Restrict financial data to `NonResidentOwner` and `BoardMember` only
- Good, because it needs no model change. - Bad, because it hides the expense register from **resident owners**, who are most of the units (~70%) and the main audience of the transparency value proposition. It defeats beneficio 2 of the brief.
## More Information
- Source of the decision: decision D1 in [02-alcance.md](../../02-alcance.md), section 7, approved by the author on 2026-11-01. - Related open questions in [05-preguntas-abiertas.md](../../05-preguntas-abiertas.md): - **Q14:** whether non-resident owners delegate to their tenants. If delegation is needed, it will be a separate, explicit grant and never an implicit consequence of `Tenant` occupancy. - **Q19:** what may be approved digitally under Ley N.° 27157. - Follow-up: under Ley N.° 27157, the board (Junta Directiva) is formed by owners. Assigning `BoardMember` should therefore require an active `Owner` occupancy. This must be confirmed in the legal review (Q19) before it becomes a validation rule. - Revisit this decision if the constitution's role set changes or if Q14 shows that delegation from owner to tenant is common. - Updated on 2026-11-02 after the QA audit ([auditoria-qa.md](../../auditoria-qa/auditoria-qa.md), findings A-02 and A-03): `EndDate` is inclusive and evaluated in `America/Lima`, and the short-lived claim alternative was removed. --- ADR-0002: --- --- status: accepted date: 2026-11-02 decision-makers: Jose Bustamante consulted: QA agent (BMAD) informed: All contributors (human and AI) ---
# Crypto-shredding for ARCO cancellation and pseudonymization on retention
## Context and Problem Statement
PRINCIPIO-004.5 of the constitution ([00-constitucion.md](../../00-constitucion.md)) requires that, 90 days after a relationship ends, `DataRetentionJob` moves personal data to an **immutable** Azure Blob Storage container (Archive tier) and deletes it from SQL Server. PRINCIPIO-004.6 requires that an accepted ARCO cancellation request is **also executed on the cold archive**. An immutable (WORM) blob cannot be deleted before its retention period expires, so both rules cannot be met literally (finding C-01).
In addition, deleting a person from SQL Server breaks operational records that reference them: who decided on a supplier hire (RN-040), who made a reservation, and who checked in a guest. "Who approved" is the core of the transparency value proposition (finding C-08).
How do we honor immutability, ARCO cancellation and record traceability at the same time?
## Decision Drivers
- Comply with PRINCIPIO-004.5 (immutable archive, deletion after 1 year) and PRINCIPIO-004.6 (cancellation also on the archive) without amending the constitution. - Keep supplier hire files complete for owners (RN-041, C-03). - Keep referential integrity of reservations, check-ins and hire decisions. - Keep the design small: one developer, 16 weeks.
## Considered Options
For the immutability vs. cancellation conflict (C-01):
1. **Crypto-shredding**: one encryption key per data subject in Azure Key Vault; cancellation destroys the key. 2. **Remove immutability** from the archive and rely on the role, the audit log and soft delete (amends PRINCIPIO-004.5). 3. **Cancellation does not touch the archive**; the archive expires after 1 year (amends PRINCIPIO-004.6; legally risky under Ley N.° 29733). 4. Leave it as an open question.
For what remains in the operational database (C-08):
1. **Pseudonymize**: keep `PersonId` and the role held at the time of the event; move personal data to the archive. 2. **Exclude decisions from retention**: keep the decision maker's name as a management record (amends PRINCIPIO-004.5). 3. Leave it as an open question.
## Decision Outcome
Chosen options: **"Crypto-shredding"** and **"Pseudonymize"**.
### Crypto-shredding
- Each data subject (person) has their own data encryption key in Azure Key Vault. - Archived records of that person are encrypted with AES-256-GCM (PRINCIPIO-005) using that key. - An accepted ARCO cancellation **destroys the person's key**. The immutable blob stays in the archive but becomes irreversibly unreadable. - The lifecycle policy still deletes the blob 1 year after archiving (PRINCIPIO-004.5).
### Pseudonymization
When `DataRetentionJob` archives a person:
- Operational records that reference them (supplier hire decisions, reservations and check-ins) **keep the `PersonId` and the role held at the time of the event**. - Personal data (name, DNI, phone, email) moves to the cold archive and is deleted from SQL Server. - Supplier hire decisions are shown to owners by role ("Junta Directiva") and date-time, not by name (C-03), so the file stays complete.
### Consequences
- Good, because immutability and cancellation are both met without a constitutional amendment. - Good, because "who approved" remains traceable (by `PersonId` and role) after retention. - Bad, because Key Vault holds one key per person (cost and key-management overhead must be checked against Q20). - Bad, because destroying a key is irreversible: a mistaken cancellation cannot be undone. - Neutral, because ARCO itself is out of the MVP scope (M-23); only the mechanism is decided here.
### Confirmation
- Integration test: archive a synthetic person, destroy their key, and verify the archived blob can no longer be decrypted while the blob itself still exists. - Integration test: after archiving a BoardMember, the hire decision still shows `decidedBy` (as `PersonId`) and the role, and no personal data of that person remains in SQL Server. - Code review checks that personal data of archived persons is never re-derivable from operational tables.
## More Information
- Findings C-01 and C-08 in [auditoria-qa.md](../../auditoria-qa/auditoria-qa.md). - Related: RN-005, RN-028 and RN-040 must be updated to state what is kept ([03-reglas-de-negocio.md](../../03-reglas-de-negocio.md)). - Open: who is the data controller (Q18) in [05-preguntas-abiertas.md](../../05-preguntas-abiertas.md); revocation of consent (Q32). - Re-audit RQ-A01 and RQ-A12 (2026-11-02): what is archived, deleted without archiving and pseudonymized for a person is fixed in RN-126 to RN-128; the audit log is encrypted and pseudonymized, never deleted while the condominium exists (RN-129, RN-130). - Second re-audit R2-C02 and R2-A04 (2026-11-02): an archived `Person` row is kept with only `PersonId` and `CondominiumId`, so references stay valid; foreign keys to `Person` use `DeleteBehavior.Restrict` in EF Core, never cascade. Account-level secrets (`PasswordHash`, TOTP secret, recovery codes) belong to the global `User` and are deleted only with the account (RN-127, RN-128). --- ADR-0003: --- --- status: accepted date: 2026-11-02 decision-makers: Jose Bustamante consulted: QA agent (BMAD) informed: All contributors (human and AI) ---
# Tenant resolution, roles per condominium and platform processes
## Context and Problem Statement
PRINCIPIO-003 restricts every query to the authenticated user's condominium through an EF Core global query filter, and forbids `IgnoreQueryFilters()` outside platform processes documented in an ADR. Several processes need cross-condominium access, but no ADR exists (finding C-07). "Current condominium" (RN-015, RN-017) is undefined for a person linked to two condominiums.
Accounts can only be created by an Administrator invitation (RN-007), so nobody can create the condominium, the first Administrator, or reset an Administrator's MFA (C-05). The second re-audit found that date-driven events (end of occupancies, automatic role revocation, account deactivation) had no authorized component (R2-A06), and that a BoardMember who loses their TOTP and recovery codes had no way back (R2-A09). The outgoing management company controls accounts, roles and `OccupancyType`, so the board cannot revoke it when the company changes (C-06), which is the core pain of the brief. Finally, it is undefined whether a user can hold several roles, who assigns `BoardMember`, and whether an Administrator who is also a BoardMember can approve their own hire (A-10).
## Decision Drivers
- Keep exactly the six roles of PRINCIPIO-006. - Keep `IgnoreQueryFilters()` limited to a closed, documented list (PRINCIPIO-003). - Let the board replace the management company without losing condominium data. - Separate the duties of the supervised party (Administrator) and the supervisors (BoardMember). - AI agents never run these processes in production (PRINCIPIO-009).
## Considered Options
Bootstrap (C-05): (1) **platform CLI process run by a human operator**; (2) seeder plus BoardMember-authorized MFA reset; (3) a new `PlatformOperator` role (amends PRINCIPIO-006); (4) open question.
Management company change (C-06): (1) **platform process at the board's request**; (2) the board does it in the app (needs a quorum, Q24); (3) open question.
Tenant resolution (C-07): (1) **global identity with a condominium selector**; (2) one account per condominium; (3) open question.
Roles (A-10): (1) **resolve all now** (multiple roles per condominium, BoardMember assigned by the platform process, Administrator/BoardMember incompatibility, residence as a declaration); (2) resolve 1–3 and leave residence open; (3) open question.
## Decision Outcome
Chosen options: **platform CLI process**, **platform process at the board's request**, **global identity with a condominium selector**, and **resolve all role questions now**.
### Platform process
- A **platform command** (CLI), not a user role, can: - create a condominium and issue the invitation for its first Administrator; - reset the MFA of an Administrator or of a BoardMember (second re-audit R2-A09); - at the board's documented request (minutes), revoke the outgoing company's accounts (its Administrator and Concierge users) and invite the new Administrator; - assign or revoke the `BoardMember` role at the board's request. - Only a **human CondoHub operator** runs it. An AI agent must not run it in production (PRINCIPIO-009). - Every run is written to the audit log. - Condominium data (registry, reservations, expenses, hires) stays with the condominium when the company changes.
### Tenant resolution
- The **user account is global**: one email and one password per person. - If a person has occupancies or roles in more than one condominium, they **choose one at sign-in**. The chosen `CondominiumId` is stored in the session and is the "current condominium" used by the global query filter, RN-015 and RN-017.
### Roles
- A user can hold **several roles**, and roles are assigned **per condominium**. - `BoardMember` is assigned only by the platform process, not by the Administrator. - `Administrator` and `BoardMember` cannot be held by the same user in the same condominium. - `Resident` or `NonResidentOwner` is assigned by the Administrator when registering the occupancy, and is revoked automatically when the person's last active occupancy in that condominium ends; other roles are unaffected (RN-060, re-audit RQ-C03). Residence is a **declaration**; the system does not verify it. - A person has one `Person` record per condominium and at most one global `User`, unique by email. Accepting an invitation links the `Person` to the `User` of that email, after signing in if the `User` already exists (RN-121, RN-122, re-audit RQ-C04).
### Closed list of processes allowed to use `IgnoreQueryFilters()`
1. Sign-in (user lookup before a condominium is chosen). 2. Invitation acceptance. 3. `DataRetentionJob`. 4. Synthetic-data seeders (non-production only, PRINCIPIO-008). 5. The platform CLI process described above. 6. `OccupancyLifecycleJob` (second re-audit R2-A06): a daily job that executes the date-driven events: end of occupancies, automatic revocation of `Resident` and `NonResidentOwner` (RN-060) and account deactivation when a person has no active occupancies or roles in any condominium (RN-073). It needs cross-condominium queries for RN-073.
Any other use is a violation of PRINCIPIO-003.
A reservation's `Completed` status (RN-085) is computed when it is read, not stored by a job, so it needs no component in this list.
### Consequences
- Good, because the six roles stay unchanged and the board can replace the management company. - Good, because the cross-tenant surface is a closed, reviewable list. - Bad, because a human operator is a single point of dependency for onboarding and company changes. - Bad, because roles per condominium make the permissions matrix larger.
### Confirmation
- A Roslyn analyzer or architecture test fails the build if `IgnoreQueryFilters()` is called outside the six allowed components. - Integration test: `OccupancyLifecycleJob` run on 2027-02-01 revokes the `Resident` role of a person whose last occupancy ended on 2027-01-31, and deactivates her account if she has no other occupancy or role in any condominium. - Integration test: a user with roles in condominiums A and B only sees A's data after choosing A. - Integration test: assigning `BoardMember` to a user who is `Administrator` in the same condominium is rejected. - Integration test: the Administrator cannot assign `BoardMember` through the API (`403`). - Every platform CLI run produces an audit log entry.

# Blind index (HMAC) for lookups and uniqueness on encrypted fields
## Context and Problem Statement
PRINCIPIO-005 requires field-level AES-256-GCM encryption for personal and contact data, including email and DNI. AES-GCM is non-deterministic: encrypting the same value twice gives different ciphertexts. The system therefore cannot find a user by email at sign-in, nor check that an email or DNI is unique. The scope ([02-alcance.md](../../02-alcance.md) §0) mentions "blind indexes or bounded searches" without deciding (finding A-13).
## Decision Drivers
- Keep every personal field encrypted (PRINCIPIO-005). - Support sign-in by email and uniqueness of email and DNI. - Avoid storing any value that can be reversed without a Key Vault key.
## Considered Options
1. **Blind index with HMAC-SHA256** stored next to the encrypted value. 2. **Email in clear text** (TDE only); violates PRINCIPIO-005 and requires an amendment. 3. Leave it as an open question (blocks M1 and M2).

- Good, because PRINCIPIO-005 is met and sign-in works. - Good, because uniqueness can be enforced with a database unique index on the blind-index column. - Bad, because the Administrator cannot search people by partial name; lookups are exact. - Bad, because rotating the HMAC key requires recomputing every blind index.
### Confirmation
- Integration test: two people with the same email (different casing or surrounding spaces) cannot be registered in the same scope. - Integration test: sign-in finds the user by email while the `Email` column contains only ciphertext. - Database check: no plaintext email or DNI exists in any table.

# Agent pull requests through a GitHub App and merge policy for the author's own pull requests
## Context and Problem Statement
PRINCIPIO-009 and PRINCIPIO-010 require at least one human approval per pull request, and GitHub does not let a person approve their own PR. CondoHub is a one-person project. Decision D2 in [02-alcance.md](../../02-alcance.md) §7 (2026-11-01) has AI agents open PRs from a project GitHub App so that the author can approve them, but it was never recorded as an ADR (PRINCIPIO-012).
Two gaps remain (finding A-18):
- The author is the only code owner and the only approver, so an agent PR that modifies `00-constitucion.md` passes if the author approves it by mistake. No CI check rejects it, even though the example in PRINCIPIO-009 says the CI does. - Nobody can approve the author's own PRs.
## Decision Drivers
- AI agents must never modify the constitution or the CI workflows (PRINCIPIO-009). - The author must be able to merge their own work in a one-person project. - Keep every quality gate (status checks) mandatory. - Keep the constitution and the CI workflows changeable by the only human author (second re-audit R2-C01).
## Considered Options
1. **CI check plus a documented exception for the author** (amends PRINCIPIO-010). 2. CI check plus a second human reviewer (for example, a classmate or teacher). 3. CI check only; the author's PR policy stays open.
## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: **"CI check plus a documented exception for the author"**.
- **Agent identity (D2):** AI agents open PRs from a project **GitHub App** with minimal permissions (branches and PRs only). The App must not be able to approve or merge PRs; this is **not verified yet**, because the `contents: write` and `pull_requests: write` permissions it needs may allow both (third re-audit R3-A01, see Confirmation). The author reviews and approves agent PRs. - **CI check:** a workflow fails, always, if the diff modifies `00-constitucion.md` or anything under `.github/workflows/` and the PR was opened by the agents' GitHub App. Every PR that changes those paths, including the author's, also requires an accepted ADR in the same PR (re-audit RQ-A11). An agent's `Co-Authored-By` trailer does **not** fail the check: it records AI assistance, and the human author is accountable for the change (second re-audit R2-A01; constitution 1.3). - **Author exception:** the human author may merge their own PRs **without approval**, only when all status checks are green. This includes changes to `00-constitucion.md` or `.github/workflows/`, which also need the accepted ADR in the same PR (second re-audit R2-C01; constitution 1.3, PRINCIPIO-009 and PRINCIPIO-010). The exception never covers PRs opened by the agents' GitHub App. - **GitHub configuration (second re-audit R2-A02):** - Two rulesets on `main`. Ruleset 1 requires all status checks, with **no bypass for anyone**. Ruleset 2 requires 1 approval, with a bypass **only for the author's account**; the GitHub App can never bypass it. Keeping them separate prevents the approval bypass from also skipping the status checks. - The protected-paths check runs from the workflow definition on `main`, not from the PR branch, so a PR cannot disable the check that should reject it. - **Not verified yet:** that GitHub behaves this way (separate rulesets with independent bypass lists, and the check running from `main`) has not been verified. Verifying it in GitHub is a **week 1 task** (see Confirmation).
- **Agent identity on GitHub (gap closed after the second re-audit, R2-A02):** an agent never pushes or opens PRs with a person's identity; it only works through the project GitHub App (PRINCIPIO-009.10, constitution 1.4). The App is installed **without** the `workflows` permission, so GitHub itself rejects any push from it that changes `.github/workflows/`. Week-1 verification: a push from the App that touches `.github/workflows/` is rejected.
### Consequences
- Good, because the constitution and workflows are protected by a technical control, not only by review. - Good, because the author is not blocked by GitHub's self-approval restriction. - Bad, because the author's own PRs get no second pair of eyes. - Bad, because it requires amending PRINCIPIO-010 (see ADR-0009).
### Confirmation
- A test PR from the GitHub App that touches `00-constitucion.md` fails the check. - A test PR from the author that touches `.github/workflows/`, with an accepted ADR, green status checks and a commit with an agent's `Co-Authored-By` trailer, can be merged without approval. - Ruleset 2 lets only the author's account bypass the approval requirement; the GitHub App can never bypass it. - Ruleset 1 keeps status checks required for every PR, including the author's, with no bypass. - **Week 1 task (not verified yet):** verify in GitHub that (a) the author's approval bypass in ruleset 2 does not skip the status checks of ruleset 1, (b) a red status check blocks the author's merge, (c) a PR that modifies the protected-paths workflow is still evaluated with the version on `main`, and (d) negative case (R3-A01): the GitHub App tries to approve a PR opened by the author and then to merge it, and GitHub rejects both actions. If GitHub does not behave this way, the work stops and the author decides a new configuration through an ADR.
## More Information

# Build `DataRetentionJob` in the MVP and defer read access to the cold archive (PIM)
## Context and Problem Statement
PRINCIPIO-004.5 requires that the cold archive can only be read with the `RetentionArchiveReader` role, activated through Microsoft Entra PIM (maximum 8 hours). PIM requires an Entra ID P2 license, which is paid. Decision D3 in [02-alcance.md](../../02-alcance.md) §7 (2026-11-01) defers PIM, but it was never recorded as an ADR (PRINCIPIO-012).
The documents also disagree on whether `DataRetentionJob` is part of the MVP: the scope (§0) says the MVP can be demonstrated without it, while RN-005 and RN-028 are MUST, and the constitution example requires a test where reading without the role returns `403` (finding A-01).
## Decision Drivers
- Remove the contradiction between the scope, the business rules and the constitution example. - Avoid a paid license (Entra ID P2) while only synthetic data exists. - Keep R7 (excessive scope) under control.
## Considered Options
1. **Job in the MVP, without archive read access.** 2. Job out of the MVP; RN-005 and RN-028 become "blockers for real data". 3. Leave it as an open question (depends on Q20).
## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: **"Job in the MVP, without archive read access"**.
- `DataRetentionJob` and the immutable cold archive (Blob Archive) are built in the MVP. - **Archive read access and PIM elevation are not implemented** (D3). No user holds `RetentionArchiveReader`, so every read attempt returns `403`, which satisfies the PRINCIPIO-004.5 example test. - RN-005 and RN-028 stay **MUST**. - Before operating with real data, the author must either acquire Entra ID P2 or amend PRINCIPIO-004.5 through the author's own PR with an accepted ADR (PRINCIPIO-010, constitution 1.3).
### Consequences
- Good, because the scope, the business rules and the constitution become consistent. - Good, because no paid license is needed during the project. - Bad, because archived data cannot be read at all until PIM (or an amendment) exists; this is acceptable only while data is synthetic. - Neutral: per ADR-0009 (M-13), PIM's cost is a budget decision (Q20), not a PRINCIPIO-002 compliance issue.
### Confirmation
- Integration test (constitution example): simulate 91 days, run `DataRetentionJob`, verify the guest no longer exists in SQL Server and exists in the Archive container. - Integration test: any attempt to read the archive returns `403`. - Release checklist: operating with real data is blocked while PIM or an amendment is missing.

# Blazor render modes and performance measurement for 3G and old phones
## Context and Problem Statement
PRINCIPIO-011 requires the app to work on old phones over 3G or slow 4G. PRINCIPIO-002 sets Blazor in Auto mode, which starts with a persistent SignalR connection and later downloads the WebAssembly runtime (several MB). There is no measurable 3G target, and the CI has no tool to measure the API p95 or the LCP required by PRINCIPIO-010 (finding A-17).
## Decision Drivers
- Meet PRINCIPIO-010 (p95 < 500 ms, LCP < 2.5 s on 4G) and PRINCIPIO-011 (3G, old phones). - Measure performance in the CI, not by hand. - Keep the stack of PRINCIPIO-002 (.NET 10, Blazor). - Use only tools allowed by PRINCIPIO-002 (no GPL or AGPL in any version, including tooling; see ADR-0009).
## Considered Options
1. **Static server-side rendering (SSR) for resident pages, targets and CI measurement.** 2. Keep Auto mode everywhere; only set targets and measurement. 3. Open question plus a performance spike in week 1.
## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: **"Static SSR for resident pages, targets and CI measurement"**.
- Resident pages use **static server-side rendering**, with interactivity only in components that need it. Auto mode is used where justified. - **3G target:** LCP < 4 s with the "Slow 3G" network profile. The 4G target of PRINCIPIO-010 (LCP < 2.5 s) stays. - **CI measurement:** - LCP with **Lighthouse CI**. - API p95 with a **load test**.
### Load-test tool (accepted by the author on 2026-11-02)
k6 was suggested during the audit but **cannot be used**: its license is AGPL-3.0, which PRINCIPIO-002 forbids in any version, and the tooling exception of ADR-0009 does not cover GPL or AGPL. The load test uses **Locust** (MIT).
### Consequences
- Good, because resident pages avoid the WebAssembly download and the persistent connection on slow networks. - Good, because performance regressions fail the CI. - Bad, because pages that mix SSR and interactive components need more design care. - Neutral, because PRINCIPIO-002 (constitution version 1.1, ADR-0009) now states that Blazor uses static server rendering and Auto mode where justified, so this decision complies with it.
### Confirmation
- Lighthouse CI runs on every PR against the resident pages with the "Slow 3G" and 4G profiles and fails above the targets. - The load test runs in the CI against the dev environment and fails if the API p95 is ≥ 500 ms. - axe still runs on every page (PRINCIPIO-010).
## More Information
- Finding A-17 in [auditoria-qa.md](../../auditoria-qa/auditoria-qa.md), including the k6 correction. - The 3G target was added to PRINCIPIO-010 in constitution version 1.1; the amendment text is in [docs/proposals/constitution-amendment-2026-11.md](../proposals/constitution-amendment-2026-11.md). --- ADR-0008: --- --- status: accepted date: 2026-11-02 decision-makers: Jose Bustamante consulted: QA agent (BMAD) informed: All contributors (human and AI) ---

- Each row is one xUnit `[Theory]` in the integration tests, with one `InlineData` per column, asserting the response code of the cell (for example, `Authz_Expenses_Read(role: R-Ten, expected: 403)`). - The tests required by ADR-0001 are covered by rows E3 and H3: `ResidentTenant_CannotReadExpenses_Returns403`, `ResidentOwner_CanReadExpenses_Returns200`, `NonResidentOwner_CanReadSupplierHires_Returns200`, `ResidentOwner_AfterOccupancyEnds_CannotReadExpenses_Returns403` and `ResidentOwner_CrossTenantExpenses_Returns404`. - The constitution's example test `Resident_CannotReadOtherUnitDebts` is covered by row S2b. - These tests count toward the 90 % coverage of the users module (PRINCIPIO-010, audit M-15).
